value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical finite projective-plane incidence graph and a natural model for landmark failure tolerance. Classifying every minimum two-fold resolving placement and the feasibility/length of optimal single-landmark redeployments addresses a meaningful metric-resolving reconfiguration gap beyond routine scalar minimization. The two completely frozen optimal bipartition placements, a connected 280-state mixed family and an exact geometrically characterized center/periphery give substantive structural information, not a trivial enumeration.
